summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was readmitted due to worsening lower extremity edema and shortness of breath, just days after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. She had a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent cellulitis, and lymphedema. Admission labs showed elevated BNP and white blood cell count, supporting fluid overload and possible infection. She was treated with IV furosemide and metolazone for aggressive diuresis, resulting in a weight loss from 151.1 kg to 144.8 kg. IV vancomycin was continued for a full 7-day course due to persistent leg redness and warmth, with improvement by discharge. Hypokalemia developed during diuresis and was managed with supplementation. Her phenytoin level rose to 26.1, prompting a dose reduction to 700 mg daily. Warfarin was increased to achieve a therapeutic INR of 2.0. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, instructions to monitor daily weight, and plans for outpatient lab follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
